work.text: Bytes held and bytes served. A miner runs a storage node with at least 2 TB behind a static public IP, keeps erasure-coded shards of customer files, answers cryptographic challenges that it still holds them, and serves reads. What is paid for is bandwidth delivered in the reporting window and shard data stored, as reported by validators on the Hippius chain.
work.quote: Miners participate in the Arion network by storing shards of encrypted user data and proving their storage continuously to the blockchain.

scoring.text: Per node: log2(bandwidth bytes + 1) weighted 70 percent plus log2(stored bytes + 1) weighted 30 percent, times uptime, minus 50 points per validator strike and 100 per integrity failure, capped at 50,000. Nodes roll up into families, one owner with many nodes: the top 10 count, each rank worth 80 percent of the one above, smoothed 30/70 against the previous value and clamped to a 100-point move per bucket.
scoring.quote: NodeBandwidthWeightPermille: u32 = 700; NodeStorageWeightPermille: u32 = 300; StrikePenalty: u16 = 50; IntegrityFailPenalty: u16 = 100

split.text: Proportional, of a sliver. The weight budget of 65,535 is split at a fixed ratio: 1 percent to storage miners, each family taking its weight over all families' weight, and 99 percent to UID 238, the Hippius validator account. A node offline past its buffer gets 0. A family seen for the first time is floored at weight 10 for 24 buckets.
split.quote: let miners_pool = max_score * 0.01; // 1% to miners; let uid_238_pool = max_score - miners_pool; // 99% to uid 238
split.disagrees: The docs page learn/weights fetched 2026-09-19, and the summary at the top of readme_weights.md, say the miner pool grows with how much data the network stores relative to emissions; the code at the pinned commit and Layer 3 of the same readme fix it at 1 percent to miners and 99 percent to UID 238.

judges.text: Twelve validators were active on the 2026-09-09 chain snapshot. Commit-reveal is off. The judging happens on Hippius's own Substrate chain: its validators submit each node's quality metrics on chain, miners cannot self-report, and pallets compute family weights and a ranked list. A Bittensor validator runs a submitter script that reads that ranked list from the Hippius chain and sets it as weights. It relays; it does not re-run the work.
judges.quote: commit_reveal_weights_enabled False, weights_rate_limit 100, max_validators 64; chain-2026-09-09.json active_validators 12

cadence.text: Emission settles every 360 blocks, about 72 minutes. The program's own clock runs on the Hippius chain at 6-second blocks: node quality is bucketed every 300 blocks, family weights and rewards recalculate every 3,600 blocks, about 6 hours, and a storage miner silent for 3,000 blocks is zeroed. A new registration is immune from deregistration for 5,000 blocks, about 16 hours.
cadence.quote: tempo 360, immunity_period 5000; readme_weights.md: Every BlocksPerEra (3,600 blocks = 6 hours at 6-second block time)

buyer.text: Anyone with a credit card or TAO. S3-compatible storage costs $6.00 per TB per month pay as you go, billed hourly, down to $4.65 per TB on a 100 TB plan, egress included. Credits are minted on the Hippius chain at one dollar each; sign-up is Google or GitHub with no wallet. No customer is named and no revenue figure is given.
buyer.quote: All services are billed per use with credits (1 credit = $1), minted on our blockchain for full visibility.

exploits.text: Splitting one operation into many nodes: the family aggregation counts only an owner's top 10 nodes with 80 percent decay per rank, and the code names the reason, log2 of parts exceeding log2 of the whole. Claiming storage not held: validator challenges issue strikes and integrity failures that subtract directly. Going dark: a node past its heartbeat buffer is zeroed. Sudden jumps: a moving average and a 100-point clamp.
exploits.quote: the same bytes across more children: log2(a) + log2(b) > log2(a+b)
